findings.issue_text: **6. `lib/post_revisor.rb:85` — silent save failure combined with unconditional sha1 update.**
**8. `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` and `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4` — `force: true` on `create_table`, plus editing an already-committed migration.**

`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:14,20` — "requires feed_polling_url"/"requires embed_by_username" only stub the setting under test and rely on `feed_polling_enabled?` defaulting to false, so they pass vacuously and would still pass if the guard were deleted.

No coverage of `poll_feed` body, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `absolutize_urls` edge cases, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, or the redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?` is stubbed out in every test that reaches it).
`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48` stubs `TopicView.new` to return `nil`, which would explode in a real render — masked by views not rendering. This is precisely why issue #1 shipped.

`app/models/topic_embed.rb:57,64` — `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, so `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg` becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.jpg` (the `sub(/^\/+/,'')` eats both slashes). Common in real feeds. Also, relative URLs without a leading slash (`images/a.png`) are left untouched. Consider `URI.join(url, href)`.

`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16` — no `raise Discourse::NotFound if @topic_view.blank?`; a deleted-but-still-referenced topic yields a nil-deref rather than a 404. Also `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches the `loading` placeholder, which is the one response you don't want cached.

`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18-20` — `feed_key` is dead code (never called). `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is an unrelated leftover. `config/locales/server.en.yml` — `embed.permalink` is never referenced.

`lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,144` — the `--category` option and `created_at: Date.parse(...)` were both dropped when switching to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. That's an undocumented CLI/behavior regression outside the PR's stated intent, and each thread now requires a live HTTP fetch with no per-thread rescue, so one dead link aborts the import.

`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17` — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin equality test; there's also no `e.source === iframe.contentWindow` check and no null guard on `#discourse-comments`. Impact is limited to iframe height, but `e.origin !== new URL(discourseUrl).origin` is just as easy.

`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10` — height is only posted on `window.onload`, so late-loading images leave the iframe mis-sized; and `loading.html.erb` polls with a 30s full page reload rather than the resize channel already in place.

`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6` — `embed_url` as default-length `string` (255) will fail on long URLs; no index on `topic_id`/`post_id`; `TopicEmbed` has no uniqueness validation, so the concurrent-import race surfaces as a raw `RecordNotUnique`.

`db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` — whitespace-only churn that also strips the trailing newline; several new files (`topic_retriever.rb`, `embed.css.scss`, both erb files) are missing trailing newlines.

No documentation anywhere for how a site owner installs `embed.js` (the `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals and the `#discourse-comments` div are entirely undocumented), and no `X-Frame-Options` note that `ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value that works only by being ignored.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found (`embed` not blank), the code does `post = embed.post` and then, if the content SHA has changed, immediately calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. Because `topic_embeds.post_id` is only a NOT NULL column (no foreign key constraint shown) and posts can be deleted/absent, `embed.post` can legitimately be `nil` (or the association can fail to load). In that case, the update path will raise (e.g., `PostRevisor` initialized with `nil`), so the import can crash for orphaned embeds. The diff contains no guard/repair for this case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **6. `lib/post_revisor.rb:85` — silent save failure combined with unconditional sha1 update.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new public route `GET /embed/best` (`config/routes.rb`) goes to `EmbedController#best`, which does not require authentication and will enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` whenever no `TopicEmbed` exists for that `embed_url`. The only gate in `ensure_embeddable` is a Referer-host check (`URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) which can be spoofed by a direct HTTP client, and `TopicRetriever` throttles only per exact `embed_url` string for 60s (redis key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can vary the path/query to bypass the throttle and enqueue many jobs and trigger many remote fetches / topic creations for the configured host. This is a concrete unauthenticated job/topic-creation amplification vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **8. `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` and `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4` — `force: true` on `create_table`, plus editing an already-committed migration.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` by changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. Editing already-committed migrations is a real correctness/process problem in Rails: environments that already ran the old migration won’t pick up the change, while new installs will, leading to divergent schemas/history. Additionally, `force: true` causes Rails to drop an existing table before creating it, which is potentially destructive if the migration is re-run or if the table exists for any reason. The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` also uses `force: true`, which carries the same drop-table risk (though it’s less problematic for a brand-new table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:14,20` — "requires feed_polling_url"/"requires embed_by_username" only stub the setting under test and rely on `feed_polling_enabled?` defaulting to false, so they pass vacuously and would still pass if the guard were deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is called only if **all** of these are true: `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, and `embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples stub only the setting under test to `nil` and do **not** stub `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` to `true` (or otherwise ensure it’s true). Since the default for `feed_polling_enabled` is `false` (per `config/site_settings.yml` in the diff), these tests will pass because the first condition fails, making them vacuous; they would still pass even if the `feed_polling_url.present?` / `embed_by_username.present?` guards were removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No coverage of `poll_feed` body, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `absolutize_urls` edge cases, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, or the redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?` is stubbed out in every test that reaches it).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed network/RSS parsing + TopicEmbed.import, TopicEmbed.import_remote with Readability/open-uri, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve including RSS-path + HTTP fetch, and retrieved_recently? Redis throttling). The added specs largely test only guard conditions (PollFeed#execute) and basic import behavior; there is no spec that executes PollFeed#poll_feed’s body, none for TopicEmbed.import_remote, and TopicRetriever specs stub retrieved_recently? in the only cases that would reach throttle logic and never exercise perform_retrieve’s internal branches. TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls is only indirectly exercised for a simple leading-slash case, with no edge-case coverage. So the “no coverage” claim is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48` stubs `TopicView.new` to return `nil`, which would explode in a real render — masked by views not rendering. This is precisely why issue #1 shipped.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" sets an expectation on `TopicView.new` (`TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})`) but does not explicitly stub a return value. While Mocha will return `nil` by default, this only affects the test's `@topic_view` assignment, not production behavior. In real execution `TopicView.new` would return a proper object, so there is no verifiable defect in the diff’s runtime code. At most, this is a test-quality concern (controller specs often don’t render views by default), not a real bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:57,64` — `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs, so `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg` becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.jpg` (the `sub(/^\/+/,'')` eats both slashes). Common in real feeds. Also, relative URLs without a leading slash (`images/a.png`) are left untouched. Consider `URI.join(url, href)`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links are rewritten when `href/src.start_with?('/')`. This condition is also true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg`. The code then does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, which strips both leading slashes, and prefixes with `"#{prefix}/"`, producing something like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.jpg` instead of preserving `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg` (or making it `http(s)://cdn...`). Additionally, relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g. `images/a.png`) are not rewritten at all, so they remain broken when embedded elsewhere. Both behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff and are realistic for feed/imported HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16` — no `raise Discourse::NotFound if @topic_view.blank?`; a deleted-but-still-referenced topic yields a nil-deref rather than a 404. Also `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches the `loading` placeholder, which is the one response you don't want cached.

adjudication.rationale:
In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally, including when no topic exists yet and the action renders the `loading` template. That means the temporary “Loading Discussion…” response can be cached for up to a minute, so repeated reloads (or intermediate caches) may keep serving the placeholder even after the topic has been retrieved — this behavior is directly implied by the diff.

However, the claim about a “nil-deref” needing `raise Discourse::NotFound if @topic_view.blank?` is not verifiable from the diff: `@topic_view` is always assigned when `topic_id` is truthy, and the failure mode for a deleted topic would more likely be an exception from `TopicView.new`/record lookup rather than `@topic_view` being nil. That part is speculative without seeing `TopicView`/exception handling.

So the caching concern is real; the nil-deref/404 part is not clearly supported by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18-20` — `feed_key` is dead code (never called). `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is an unrelated leftover. `config/locales/server.en.yml` — `embed.permalink` is never referenced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `feed_key` is defined in `Jobs::PollFeed` but not used within that file/class; however the finding’s stronger claim that it is “dead code (never called)” cannot be verified from the diff alone because it could be invoked externally. Similarly, `require_dependency 'email/sender'` in `retrieve_topic.rb` appears unused in that file, but calling it an “unrelated leftover” is subjective and not a demonstrable defect. Finally, `embed.permalink` is not referenced in the newly added embed views, but asserting it is “never referenced” across the app cannot be verified from the diff. Overall, the finding overstates what can be proven from the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,144` — the `--category` option and `created_at: Date.parse(...)` were both dropped when switching to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. That's an undocumented CLI/behavior regression outside the PR's stated intent, and each thread now requires a live HTTP fetch with no per-thread rescue, so one dead link aborts the import.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category` and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. It also drops `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` when creating the topic/post. Instead it now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which performs a live `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` with no rescue; failures like HTTP errors/timeouts would raise and abort the import loop. These are concrete behavior/CLI regressions and a new failure mode introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10` — height is only posted on `window.onload`, so late-loading images leave the iframe mis-sized; and `loading.html.erb` polls with a 30s full page reload rather than the resize channel already in place.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe posts its height on `window.onload`. In browsers, `window.onload` fires only after all subresources (including images) have finished loading, so “late-loading images leave the iframe mis-sized” is not a directly verifiable defect from this diff (absent lazy-loading/dynamic DOM changes, which aren’t shown). Also, `loading.html.erb`’s 30s full page reload is a deliberate polling mechanism to transition from the loading view to the real embed once the background job finishes; the existing postMessage “resize channel” is for communicating height to the parent, not for detecting when the topic is ready. So the finding is largely speculative/design critique rather than a clear bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6` — `embed_url` as default-length `string` (255) will fail on long URLs; no index on `topic_id`/`post_id`; `TopicEmbed` has no uniqueness validation, so the concurrent-import race surfaces as a raw `RecordNotUnique`.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as a plain `string` (Rails default 255) and adds a **unique** index on it. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a read-then-create pattern (`where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) without any rescue, and `TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve` also checks `exists?` before importing. Under concurrent imports of the same URL, this can race and surface as an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` from the DB unique index. Also, using a 255-length `string` for URLs can indeed fail for longer URLs (DB insert error/truncation depending on adapter), which is a plausible correctness issue given this column is meant to store arbitrary embed URLs. The lack of indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id` is more of a performance suggestion than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` — whitespace-only churn that also strips the trailing newline; several new files (`topic_retriever.rb`, `embed.css.scss`, both erb files) are missing trailing newlines.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show whitespace-only changes in `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` and multiple files marked with `\ No newline at end of file` (e.g., `embed.css.scss`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, and the modified migration). However, these are formatting/style issues rather than a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change; Ruby/Rails will run fine without a trailing newline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No documentation anywhere for how a site owner installs `embed.js` (the `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals and the `#discourse-comments` div are entirely undocumented), and no `X-Frame-Options` note that `ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value that works only by being ignored.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `embed.js` that relies on global variables (`discourseUrl`, `discourseEmbedUrl`) and a `#discourse-comments` element, but the claim that there is “no documentation anywhere” is not verifiable from this diff alone (docs could exist elsewhere outside the changed files). Likewise, the complaint about “no X-Frame-Options note” is primarily about missing documentation; while the code does set `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"` (a non-standard value), the finding as written is about the lack of an explanatory note rather than identifying a concrete functional/security defect proven by the diff.
